summary.title: Full Stack Fest: Architectural Patterns of Resilient Distributed Systems
summary.one_liner: A talk-slide deck on architectural and operational patterns (redundancy, decomposition, circuit breakers, versioning, fault injection) for building resilient distributed systems.
takeaways: Build failure domain independence and decompose systems so only subsystems that need strong consistency pay for it.
Use circuit breakers, per-dependency thread pools, backpressure, timeouts, and load shedding to contain failures.
Version APIs, protocols, and disk formats from the start, and treat configuration as an interface operators will use.
Reduce risk with canaries, feature flags, dark deploys, fault injection, and runbooks linked to alerts.
summary.summary: This Speaker Deck page hosts the slides for a Full Stack Fest 2016 talk on resilient distributed systems, with a link to a companion GitHub repo. The text is a condensed set of slide fragments rather than full prose, so the details are sparse. It covers patterns such as probabilistic availability, decomposition and orthogonality, circuit breakers, bulkheads, versioning, checksums, and gossip/anti-entropy, alongside operational practices like canaries, fault injection, feature flags, and runbooks. It also discusses Cook's model of system safety and questions to ask about redundancy and on-call readiness.
